## Answers to specific questions

Each of these cites the statute, administrative rule or county page it relies on.

- [Does Oregon require a well test when you sell a house?](https://larissamayfieldre.com/answers/oregon-well-test-required-to-sell.html): Yes. Under ORS 448.271, if the property you are selling has a well that supplies ground water for domestic use, you must have it tested for arsenic, nitrate and total coliform bacteria once you accept an offer. The sample has to be analysed by an accredited laboratory, and you must give the results to the buyer and file them with the Oregon Health Authority within 90 days of receiving them. Results stay valid for one year, so if a sale falls through you can reuse them on the next offer. Spring wells, irrigation-only wells and wells on undeveloped land are exempt.
- [What if there's no septic permit on file for a property?](https://larissamayfieldre.com/answers/septic-no-permit-on-file-lane-county.html): You get an Existing System Evaluation Report. When a property has a septic system but no as-built drawing or permit in the county record, that report is how the system gets documented — completed by a licensed installer, on the DEQ form, and filed with Lane County Land Management. It is not a pass/fail inspection and it does not create a permit retroactively. It tells you what is in the ground, whether it appears to be functioning, and what you would be taking on.
- [If I sell land that's in farm or forest deferral, do I owe the back taxes?](https://larissamayfieldre.com/answers/farm-forest-deferral-additional-tax-when-you-sell.html): Usually not, and this is the single most misunderstood thing about rural land in Oregon. Selling is not what triggers the additional tax — changing the use is. Under ORS 308A.706 the tax stays a potential liability, unimposed, as long as the land is not being converted to residential, commercial or industrial use. A buyer who keeps farming it or keeps it in forest simply carries the deferral forward. When it is disqualified and converted, ORS 308A.703 sets the reach-back: ten years for exclusive-farm-use farmland that stays outside an urban growth boundary, five if it is inside one, five for farmland in a non-EFU zone, and five for designated forestland — never more years than the land actually held the assessment.
- [How do I find the well log for a property?](https://larissamayfieldre.com/answers/find-well-log-oregon.html): Search the Oregon Water Resources Department's well report database at apps.wrd.state.or.us/apps/gw/well_log. It is free, it is public, and it holds drilling records for most wells drilled in Oregon since the mid-1950s. The easiest route is to enter the street address, which auto-fills the township-range-section, then browse the wells in that section. You can also search by county, by well log ID, by tax lot, or by the driller's name. What you get back is a scan of the report the driller filed when the well went in — depth, construction, what they hit, and what it produced on the day it was drilled.
- [How many bedrooms is my septic approved for, and can I add one?](https://larissamayfieldre.com/answers/septic-bedrooms-approved-add-a-bedroom.html): Your septic permit states the design capacity, and that number — not the zoning, not the lot size — is usually what caps the bedroom count. Oregon sizes residential systems by bedrooms: under OAR 340-071-0220 a dwelling with four or fewer bedrooms needs a septic tank of at least 1,000 gallons, and more than four bedrooms requires at least 1,500. You cannot simply add a bedroom. Under OAR 340-071-0210 nobody may alter or increase an existing system's design capacity without a permit first — an alteration permit if the increase stays within the greater of 300 gallons per day or 50% of existing capacity, and a full construction-installation permit if it goes beyond that.
- [Do water rights come with the land when I buy it?](https://larissamayfieldre.com/answers/water-rights-transfer-with-land-oregon.html): A certificated water right is appurtenant to the land under ORS 540.510 — it attaches to the ground, and on a sale it is treated as included unless the seller expressly reserves it in the deed or sale contract. A water right permit is not yet vested and so is not legally appurtenant, though because it names a specific place of use it usually follows the land too. Two things matter more than the transfer question: the right runs with that land and cannot be moved to other property without a formal transfer application, and under ORS 540.610 five successive years of non-use raises a rebuttable presumption of forfeiture. A right nobody has exercised since 2015 may not be a right any more.
- [I own bare EFU land. Can I build a house on it?](https://larissamayfieldre.com/answers/lot-of-record-dwelling-efu-oregon.html): Not automatically, and owning the land is not the qualifying fact. Exclusive farm use zoning exists to keep farmland farmed, so a dwelling has to fit one of the narrow routes the statutes allow. The one that catches most bare parcels is the lot of record dwelling under ORS 215.705, and it turns on history rather than acreage: the lot must have been lawfully created, the tract must have no dwelling on it already, and the present owner must have acquired it before 1 January 1985 — or received it by will or intestate succession from someone who did. If you bought it in 2019, that route is closed to you, no matter how the parcel is shaped or what the neighbours have.
- [Is a manufactured home real property or personal property?](https://larissamayfieldre.com/answers/manufactured-home-real-or-personal-property-oregon.html): It depends on whether it has been recorded in the county deed records under ORS 446.626. Until it is, a manufactured home is titled personal property — closer to a vehicle than a house — and it is financed, insured and conveyed differently. To record it, the owner must own the land beneath it, hold a recorded leasehold of 20 years or more that expressly permits recording, or be a member of a qualifying nonprofit cooperative that owns the land. One nuance that trips people: recording is independent of how the assessor taxes it. Recording governs conveyance, mortgages and liens; the tax classification is a separate determination.

## Service areas

- [Veneta](https://larissamayfieldre.com/communities/veneta.html): Small-town roots, ten minutes from Eugene.
- [Elmira](https://larissamayfieldre.com/communities/elmira.html): Quiet acreage living, close to everything.
- [Eugene](https://larissamayfieldre.com/communities/eugene.html): Oregon's second city — culture meets nature.
- [Springfield](https://larissamayfieldre.com/communities/springfield.html): Affordable homes, growing opportunity.
- [Junction City](https://larissamayfieldre.com/communities/junction-city.html): Farmland and heritage in the heart of the valley.
- [Cottage Grove](https://larissamayfieldre.com/communities/cottage-grove.html): Covered bridges and forested hills.
- [Oakridge](https://larissamayfieldre.com/communities/oakridge.html): Mountain biking capital of the Northwest.
- [Creswell](https://larissamayfieldre.com/communities/creswell.html): Family-friendly and freeway-close.
- [Drain](https://larissamayfieldre.com/communities/drain.html): Timber country with room to breathe.
- [Lane County](https://larissamayfieldre.com/communities/lane-county.html): From the ocean to the Cascades.
- [Linn County](https://larissamayfieldre.com/communities/linn-county.html): Grass seed capital and Cascade foothills.
- [Benton County](https://larissamayfieldre.com/communities/benton-county.html): Corvallis, Oregon State, and rolling hills.
- [Douglas County](https://larissamayfieldre.com/communities/douglas-county.html): Umpqua Valley — wine, timber, and wide open land.
